711101.t: From a Proto-Indo-European *puH-ro-s (“corn, wheat”), also reflected in Lithuanian pū́ras (“single winter corn”), Proto-Slavic *py̑rь (“dog-grass”), and Old English fyrs (idem).

711135.t: Of unclear origin. Perhaps from a Proto-Indo-European *wr̥b-, with cognates such as Lithuanian virbas, Old Church Slavonic врьба (vrĭba) (Russian верба (verba)) and Latin verbēnae.

711121.t: A frozen ablative form from πο- (po-) (from the base of Proto-Indo-European *kʷos) + -ως (-ōs, adverb ending). See also πως (pōs).

711148.t: From Proto-Hellenic *wrāhi- (a variant of *wrāha, whence ῥᾶ (rhâ, “easily”)), of undetermined etymology, followed by a suffixed *-gʷy-o-s, from Proto-Indo-European *gʷey- (“force”) (whence also βία (bĭ́ā, “violence; force”)).

711115.t: Probably Pre-Greek, but see Proto-Indo-European *peh₂ǵ- (“to attach, fix”).

711117.t: From Proto-Indo-European *pōlH-o-s, from *pelH- (“young animal”). Compare Latin pullus.

711158.t: From Proto-Indo-European *uh₁r-. Cognates include Latin ūrīnor, Old Armenian գայռ (gayṙ), and Sanskrit वार् (vā́r), वारि (vā́ri).

711185.t: Of unclear origin. Traditionally derived from Proto-Indo-European *werb- (“to bend, turn”), and compared with Latin verber (“lash, whip”), Proto-Germanic *warpą (“warp”), but this is phonetically impossible.

711172.t: The word may belong with ῥάβδος (rhábdos, “rod, wand”) and cognates. According to Beekes, it is quite probably a Pre-Greek word.

711160.t: Clear morphological cognates lacking outside Greek. The traditional comparison with Sanskrit वृश्चति (vṛścati, “to hew, cleave”) is not accepted by Beekes.

711179.t: From the root of ῥαίνω (rhaínō, “to sprinkle”) + -τός (-tós).

711183.t: From ῥαπίζω (rhapízō, “to strike, thrash, cudgel, hit, slap”) + -μα (-ma).

711182.t: Possibly from ῥέπω (rhépō, “to let fall, drop, decline, descend”) + -ίζω (-ízō); related to ῥαπίς (rhapís), ῥάβδος (rhábdos, “rod, staff”).
